summary: For each day, find how many days until a warmer temperature (0 if none).
mainInsight: Keep a stack of indices of days still waiting for a warmer day, with non-increasing temperatures. A new warmer day resolves (pops) every colder waiting day at once.

approaches.name: Monotonic decreasing stack
approaches.summary: Pop colder indices when a warmer temperature appears and record the distance.

approaches.name: Backward scan with jumps
approaches.summary: Iterate from the right, jump via already-computed answers.

promptVariants: Which pattern solves 'next greater element' type questions?
What technique finds the next warmer day for every index?
options: Sliding window that expands until a larger value is found
Binary search over the sorted values for the next larger one
Two pointers moving in from both ends of the array
cards.explanation: Indices waiting for a greater value are kept on a stack and resolved as soon as it appears.

promptVariants: What does the stack contain at any time and why are the temperatures non-increasing from bottom to top?
State the invariant of the monotonic stack.
cards.answer: It holds the indices of days that have not yet found a warmer day, with temperatures non-increasing from bottom to top: any day colder than a later one would already have been popped when the later one arrived.
keyPoints: Colder days popped by a warmer day
cards.explanation: When a warmer day arrives it resolves the whole run of colder tops.

promptVariants: Time complexity of the monotonic stack solution: ___
Complete the statement: Time complexity of the monotonic stack solution: ___
cards.explanation: Each index is pushed once and popped at most once.

promptVariants: What is the worst case for the stack size?
For which input does the Daily Temperatures stack grow to its maximum size?
cards.answer: O(n): a non-increasing temperature sequence (e.g. 90, 80, 70, ...) never pops, so every index stays on the stack.
cards.explanation: The answer array is also O(n).

promptVariants: Why `<` and not `<=` in `t[stack[-1]] < t[i]`, and how is the answer computed?
cards.answer: We need a STRICTLY warmer day, so equal temperatures must stay on the stack. i - idx is the number of days between the waiting day idx and the first warmer day i. Days left on the stack at the end keep the default 0.
cards.explanation: Using <= would wrongly resolve equal temperatures.

promptVariants: How does an increasing sequence behave?
cards.explanation: Each day is followed by a warmer day the very next day, except the last one, which has none (0).

incorrectOptionExplanations.[0,0,0,0,0]: There are warmer days ahead, so only the last entry is 0.
incorrectOptionExplanations.[4,3,2,1,0]: That counts the days to the final day instead of the next warmer day.
incorrectOptionExplanations.[1,1,1,1,1]: The last day has no warmer day after it, so its entry is 0.
